title: Monte Carlo simulation for stress‑free film
action: Construct the effective Hamiltonian for PbZrO₃ using the parameters from Ref [24]. Set up a 12×12×12 supercell film with 5 nm thickness, growth direction [001], in‑plane periodic boundary conditions, and surface charge screening parameter β=0.975. Run simulated annealing Monte Carlo from 955 K down to 5 K in steps of 25 K, equilibrating each temperature with 40,000 sweeps. For each temperature, apply an external electric field along the growth direction at values 50, 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600 kV/cm and record the polarization hysteresis loop (P–E). Save the raw polarization data as raw_PE_stress_free.npz.
description: Produces the raw polarization loops for the stress‑free film, required by the downstream electrocaloric analysis.

title: Monte Carlo simulation for strained film
action: Run the same simulated annealing Metropolis Monte Carlo protocol as step 1, but for a film under −1.5 % compressive epitaxial strain (in‑plane strain imposed) and screening parameter β=0.98. Save the raw polarization data as raw_PE_strained.npz.
description: Produces the raw polarization loops for the compressively strained film, required by the downstream electrocaloric analysis.

title: Electrocaloric ΔT and ΔS for stress‑free film
action: Load the raw polarization data from the stress‑free simulation. For each electric field and temperature, extract the upper branch (P>0) of the hysteresis loop to obtain P(T). Smooth the P(T) curves using Bezier interpolation. Numerically differentiate to obtain (∂P/∂T)_E. Integrate the Maxwell relations ΔT = −1/ρ ∫₀^E (T/C)(∂P/∂T)_E dE and ΔS = −1/ρ ∫₀^E (∂P/∂T)_E dE with ρ=8.3 g/cm³ and C=302 J/(kg·K). Write the resulting ΔT and ΔS for all temperatures (5 K to 955 K in steps of 25 K) and all fields (50,100,200,300,400,500,600 kV/cm) to /app/outputs/deltaT_stress_free.csv.
description: CSV file containing the electrocaloric temperature change ΔT and isothermal entropy change ΔS for the stress‑free film at all temperatures and applied fields.
output_schema: CSV with columns: temperature (K), field (kV/cm), deltaT (K), deltaS (J/kg·K). Rows: all temperatures 5–955 K in 25 K steps (39 values) for each field, sorted by temperature then field.

title: Electrocaloric ΔT and ΔS for strained film
action: Load raw_PE_strained.npz and perform exactly the same extraction, smoothing, differentiation, and integration as step 3. Write the ΔT and ΔS results to /app/outputs/deltaT_strained.csv.
description: CSV file containing ΔT and ΔS for the compressively strained film at all temperatures and applied fields.
output_schema: Same format as deltaT_stress_free.csv: temperature (K), field (kV/cm), deltaT (K), deltaS (J/kg·K).
